latest_release.body:
Appwrite 2.7.1 is a security release that moves the Open Runtimes executor to 1.3.1. It ships with the same 1.2.138 self-hosted Console as 2.7.0, has no schema changes, and upgrading from 2.7.0 only replaces the images.

### Security

- Update the Open Runtimes executor from 1.1.2 to 1.3.1 (open-runtimes/executor#269, #15310). Executor 1.1.2 followed symlinks that a function or site plants in its execution log files, build logs, build output or build cache, and it used the runtime's log id without checking it. A function could read files from the executor container, including its environment with `_APP_EXECUTOR_SECRET`, as its own logs or build output. With that secret, code in a function can call the executor API directly, and the executor controls Docker on the host. **You are affected if anyone you don't fully trust can deploy functions or sites on your instance.** Upgrade, then rotate `_APP_EXECUTOR_SECRET` if that applies to you.
- Executor 1.2.x and 1.3.x also bring changes that keep existing behaviour: `OPR_EXECUTOR_SECRET_PREVIOUS` for rotating the executor secret without downtime, a storage DSN check that is off by default, and an opt-in streamed response format.

### Install

```bash
docker run -it --rm \
    --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    --volume "$(pwd)"/appwrite:/usr/src/code/appwrite:rw \
    --entrypoint="install" \
    appwrite/appwrite:2.7.1
```

### Upgrade

Upgrading from 2.7.0 uses the same command with `--entrypoint="upgrade"`, then run the migration, which has nothing to change for this release:

```bash
cd appwrite
docker compose exec appwrite migrate
```

If you maintain your own `docker-compose.yml`, set the `openruntimes-executor` image to `openruntimes/executor:1.3.1` and run `docker compose up -d`.

To rotate the executor secret, set a new `_APP_EXECUTOR_SECRET` in `.env` and run `docker compose up -d`. This recreates the API, the workers and the executor together, so nothing needs the old value.

**Back up your data first.**

### Contributors

Thank you to everyone who contributed to 2.7.1:

@loks0n

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/compare/2.7.0...2.7.1

detail.readme_excerpt:
Appwrite

The open-source cloud for agents and developers. Appwrite is an MCP and agent-first platform for building and scaling apps. Give your agents Auth, Databases, Storage, Functions, Messaging, Realtime, and Hosting, all in one place.

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://appwrite.io/discord) [![X](https://img.shields.io/badge/follow-000000?style=flat-square&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/appwrite) [![Appwrite Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cloud-F02E65?style=flat-square&logo=icloud&logoColor=white)](https://cloud.appwrite.io) English | [简体中文](README-CN.md) Appwrite is an MCP and agent-first, open-source platform for building and scaling apps. MCP is included, so coding agents can operate on a live Appwrite project. Appwrite is available as a managed cloud platform and can also be self-hosted on infrastructure you control. It is designed for the AI agents in your workflow as well as for developers. Connect Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and other agents through the hosted MCP server, or integrate an SDK into your app. Modular products stay unified from the first prototype to production scale. Find out more at [https://appwrite.io](https://appwrite.io).
